By the present Appeal, the Appellant has challenged the Judgment and Order dated 14/10/2009 passed by the Joint Civil Judge Senior Division, Buldhana in Land Acquisition Case No. 391/1998.

3. It is the submission of the Appellant that the learned Reference Court failed to consider the documents which are placed on record, and therefore, seeks indulgence of this Court in the matter for the enhancement of compensation amount.

4. The undisputed facts in the present Appeal are as under :
The Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for acquisition of land for Pentakali Project was issued on 10/4/1997.
Accordingly, by Award dated 18/2/1998, the land owned by the Appellant bearing Gat No.2, situated at Warkhed, Tahsil Chikhli, District Buldhana, admeasuring 1.71 HR was acquired for the said project.
In the final Award, the compensation at the rate of Rs.63,230/- per hectare was awarded to the Appellant.
5. Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer, the Appellant preferred reference proceeding and sought enhancement of the compensation amount.
However, by the impugned 3/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt Judgment and Award dated 18/2/1998, the learned Reference Court has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.65,000/- per hectare.
6. In the background of this factual position, Appellant has preferred the present Appeal before this Court.

It is the submission of the Appellant that he has placed on record, before the Reference Court,
the certified copy of the Judgment dated 28/3/2008 passed by the Civil Judge Senior Division,
Buldhana in LAC No. 399/98.
The said proceeding was arising out of the same acquisition proceeding and the Reference Court has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.95,000/- per hectare.
According to the Appellant, the Reference Court has neither considered all material documents nor discussed about the same in the impugned Judgment.
Hence, the same is liable to be quashed and set aside.

7. The learned Counsel for Appellant, during the course of hearing, has placed on record the pursis informing about filing of the certified copy of Judgment dated 25/8/2009 delivered by the Civil Judge Senior Division, Buldhana in LAC NO. 395/1998, which was also arising out of the same acquisition proceeding, wherein the compensation was awarded at the rate of Rs.95,000/- per hectare to the Claimant therein.

Hence, on the basis of this documentary evidence, it is the submission of the Appellant that compensation 4/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt awarded by the Reference Court needs modification to the extent of Rs.95,000/- per hectare.
8.
The learned Counsel for Respondent No.3 has strongly opposed the Appeal.
It is his contention that it was the duty of the Appellant to refer the certified copy of Judgment in LAC No. 399/1998 before the Reference Court.
He pointed out that in the certified copy of Judgment in LAC No.399/1998 (Exhibt-30), the land involved therein was having a well and pipeline.

Therefore,

sentences.text: 2 Reference Court has enhanced the amount of compensation to the extent of Rs.95,000/- per hectare by treating the said land as an irrigated land.
Therefore, the Judgment, which is relied upon by the Appellant is not helpful to him in the present matter.

Insofar as the Judgment dated 25/8/2009 delivered in LAC No.395/1998, which is placed on record by the Appellant during the course of hearing is concerned, it is the submission of learned Counsel for the Respondent No.3 that unless the said Judgment is being a part and parcel of the record before the Reference Court, same cannot be considered at this stage.
Hence, on this submission, prayer is made to dismiss the Appeal.
9. I have heard learned Counsel for both sides and gone through the 5/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt record.
Prima facie it is crystal clear that the Judgment, which the Appellant has relied upon, was a part and parcel of the reference proceeding, because same was duly exhibited before the Reference Court.
Therefore, the Reference Court ought to have referred the said Judgment while considering the reference proceeding.
But the bare perusal of the impugned order shows that there is not at all consideration of the Judgment, which the Appellant has relied upon.

It is specifically pointed out by the Appellant from the Judgment that though there was a well and pipeline in the land involved in LAC No.399/1998, the Reference Court has discarded the said fact by recording the finding that no sufficient evidence about the well and pipeline, which was stated to be available in the field, has been produced on record by the Claimant therein.
Hence, the learned Reference Court has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.95,000/- per hectare, by considering the quality, fertility and potentiality of the land.
10. As far as the Judgment in LAC No. 395/1998, which is produced during the course of hearing is concerned, it will be relevant to consider Section 51-A of the Land Acquisition Act.

In support of this, it will be relevant to refer the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of Cement Corporation of India Ltd. V/s Purya and Others, (2004) 8 Supreme 6/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt Court Cases 270, particularly, paragraph Nos. 26 and 27, which read thus :
"26.

entities.text: Cement Corporation of India Ltd. V/s Purya and Others, (2004) 8 Supreme 6/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt Court Cases 270
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the acquisition proceedings, sale deeds are required to be brought on record for the purpose of determining market value payable to the owner of the land when it is sought to be acquired.

27. Although by reason of the aforementioned provision the parties are free to produce original documents and prove the same in accordance with the terms of the rules of evidence as envisaged under the Indian Evidence Act, the LA Act provides for an alternative thereto by inserting the said provision in terms whereof the certified copies which are otherwise secondary evidence may be brought on record evidencing a transaction.
Such transactions in terms of the aforementioned provision may be accepted in evidence.
Acceptance of an evidence is not a term of art.
It has an etymological meaning.
It envisages exercise of judicial mind to the materials on record.
Acceptance of evidence by a court would be dependent upon the facts of the case and other relevant factors.

A piece of evidence in a given situation may be accepted by a court of law but in another it may not be."

According to this provision, the certified copy of documents can be produced in any proceeding and same can be accepted by the Court
, therefore, I am of the opinion that certified copy of Judgment dated 25/8/2009 in LAC No.395/1998 can be considered in the present matter.

11. On bare perusal of the Judgment in LAC No. 395/1998, it will be relevant to consider the fact that the Reference Court, while reaching to the conclusion for enhancement of compensation, has considered the sale 7/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt transaction of village Ghanmodi, and accordingly, on the basis of the sale transaction, reached to the conclusion that the Claimant therein is entitled for the compensation at the rate of Rs.95,000/- per hectare.
12.

The learned Counsel for Appellant has pointed out from the copy of final Award that under the caption of "valuation of agricultural land", there is a specific mention that to consider proper and appropriate market value of the land, the Acquiring Body has considered the sale transaction of villages Ghanmodi, Manmodi and Borakhedi while passing the Award.
In view of this fact, the learned Reference Court in LAC No. 395/1998 has relied upon the sale instance of Ghanmodi, which cannot be said to be incorrect in the facts and circumstances of the case.

13. The Appellant, in support of his submission has relied upon the Judgment of this Court in the case of Mohd. Mustak Mohammad Ismail V/s Special Land Acquisition Officer, Collector Office,
Amravati and others, 2017(5) Mh.L.J. 600, wherein this Court, by relying upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, has observed in paragraph Nos.15 and 16 as under :
"15.

sentences.text:
The legal position as crystallised by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the authority is thus to the effect that the land owner should get 8/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt actual market value of the land acquired and no technicalities should come in his way in getting the actual market value.
16.

In subsequent decision of Imrat Lal and others vs Land Acquisition Collector and others, 2014(9) Scale 446, it was further held that, even if the landowners may not have been able to seek intervention of this Court for grant of enhanced compensation due to illiteracy, poverty and ignorance, they should not be deprived of the benefit of enhanced compensation which is awarded to other landowners from the same village whose lands are acquired under the same Award.

entities.text: Imrat Lal and others vs Land Acquisition Collector and others, 2014(9) Scale 446
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the Hon'ble Supreme Court was pleased to issue direction that those who have not filed special leave petition should also be given enhanced compensation."

14. In the light of abovesaid factual position, in the present Appeal, undisputedly the land of the Appellant at Warkhed comes under the adjacent place of Borakhedi and same is acquired by the final Award, I am of the opinion that the Reference Court committed error by not considering the sale instances by which market value of land was determined of those, whose land was acquired from same acquisition proceeding.

15. In the circumstance, considering the fact that the Appellant's land being dry crop land and the documents, which the Appellant has placed on record, particularly Exhibit-30, shows that there was Ramrao S/O Deorao Bhagat vs The State Of Mah.

a well and pipeline meaning thereby that water resource was available in the said land.

Therefore,
considering the overall factual position, Appellant is entitled for enhancement 9/9 43-B.Judg.fa.243.2010.odt at the rate of Rs. 80,000/- per hectare.
Resultantly, the following order is passed.
ORDER 1.
First Appeal is allowed.

2. The Judgment and Order dated 14/10/2009 passed by the Joint Civil Judge Senior Division,
Buldhana in Land Acquisition Case No. 391/1998 is quashed and set aside.
3.
The Respondents are directed to pay enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs.80,000/- per hectare to the Appellant along with statutory benefits within a period of three months.

4. The Respondents are further directed to deposit the enhanced amount by deducting the amount which is already paid, either before this Court or before the Reference Court, with due intimation to the Appellant.
5. The Appellant will be at liberty to withdraw the amount after the same is deposited.
6. No order as to costs.
